answer: A cheap sybil defense meters ingress, not keys. Each agent receives a dedicated data inlet: a unicast feed of signed readings unique per key, billed against its deposit. Hourly the registry demands the byte at a random stream offset. A farm relaying one feed to a thousand aliases fails, since all observed identical bytes; a thousand inlets costs a thousand bills. Collusion profits only while separate ingress stays cheaper than per-alias reward. It is a marble through pipes: each key's path is physically its own, and no fable of shared ownership hides the inlet it entered by.
